title: Asymmetric critic implemented behind --asym-critic
hypothesis: critic sees hole - tip (xy) and depth; the actor sees only sensors, so the deployed policy stays unprivileged
result: unit test: critic fits a reward that depends only on the privileged input (TD error -80 %), actor input unchanged; smoke run with demos OK. Not launched: the machine is busy with R1

title: Demos with a BC floor (2.5 -> 1.0, never 0), F/T x5
hypothesis: the R1 collapse happens when BC reaches 0; a floor keeps the demo-level behaviour while RL improves on it
note: best recipe so far, bar narrowly missed; the two failures (seeds 1, 3) fell into dive-and-abort early (best checkpoints at 80k and 20k)
result: F/T 45, 7, 44, 6, 44 /50: 3 of 5 seeds at 88-90 % (bar needs 4), mean 58.4 % (baseline 25.6 %, R1 38.8 %); winners insert in ~32 steps, peak force < 50 N

title: Asymmetric critic alone (no demos), F/T x5
hypothesis: a critic that sees hole - tip gives the actor a useful gradient before it can find the hole by chance
note: --asym-critic stays off (default 0) and is not combined in R3
result: F/T 12, 17, 7, 6, 13 /50, mean 22 % vs baseline 25.6 %: no benefit

title: Stronger imitation: BC 5.0 -> floor 2.5 (R1b recipe otherwise), F/T seeds 0-4
hypothesis: the failing seeds dive because the BC term is too weak against the Q term; doubling it keeps them on the demo behaviour
result: F/T 45, 8, 26, 49, 46 /50 (same seeds as R1b: 45, 7, 44, 6, 44): 3 of 5 at >= 80 %, mean 69.6 % vs 58.4 %; rescued seed 3 (6 -> 49), seed 1 still dives early, seed 2 still climbing at 150k

title: R1b recipe on 5 more seeds (5-9)

note: same runs dir as R1b; seeds 5-9
result: seeds 5-9: 50, 35, 25, 50, 5 /50. R1b over 10 seeds: 5 of 10 at >= 80 %, mean 62.2 %; every failure is an early dive-and-abort (best checkpoints at 20-80k)

title: Offline TD3+BC pretraining on the demos before interaction (probe)
hypothesis: an actor pretrained on demos starts competent, so RL never passes through the dive-and-abort phase
result: rejected on probes, not launched: pretrained actors abort in 10/10 episodes even with the Q term off (BC loss 0.0004). Trace: imitation is fine on expert states, but (1) the expert's own rim contact is 35-42 N against a 60 N abort, so a slightly faster approach (-0.26 vs -0.17) aborts, and (2) the one-step 0.5 mm correction regresses to ~0.1 (Lesson 2 again)
note: --pretrain-steps / --pretrain-q-weight stay at 0 / 1 (off). Q-extrapolation hypothesis also rejected along the way

title: R3a recipe (BC 5.0 -> 2.5) on seeds 5-9
hypothesis: 10-seed estimate of the stronger-imitation recipe, to compare with R1b's 5/10
note: imitation strength is not the lever; the failures are the same early dive-and-abort (one hover-timeout). R1b recipe kept as the base

title: Rim speed limit (0.5 mm/step within 5 mm of the rim) + R1b recipe, seeds 0-9
hypothesis: every failed run collapses into dive-and-abort; a controller-level speed limit near contact (known rim height, not privileged; the expert's own contact speed) removes that basin, so RL spends its budget on the lateral search
note: the dive was a symptom, not the cause: without it the failed runs still never learn the lateral search and hover until timeout. --rim-speed-limit-mm stays 0 (off)
result: 46, 12, 13, 32, 10, 43, 44, 15, 10, 12 /50: 3/10 at >= 80 %, mean 47.4 % (R1b on the same seeds: 5/10, 62.2 %). Failures turned from force aborts into timeouts

title: xy_abs actions for TD3 (lateral target within +-5 mm of the start), R1b recipe, seeds 0-9
hypothesis: the failed runs never learn the lateral correction, which as a delta is a one-step pulse that BC and the actor average to ~0 (Lesson 2); as a position it is a persistent step
note: as on the gantry, a position target carries per-step regression error (~0.1-0.25 mm) that is too coarse for 0.5 mm clearance. --action-mode stays delta
result: finished seeds: 19, 11, 0, 1, 0, 0, 3, 8 /50 (2 still running, late evals 10-20 %): far below R1b; most runs hover until timeout

title: V1 ISO fasteners, hole block, bin and bucket (src/fvb/envs/fasteners.py)
result: M16x50 bolt (ISO 4017, 118 g) and M16 nut (ISO 4032) within 0.1 mm / 5 % mass; 17 mm fine hole with 1 mm chamfer seats bolts at 0 and 1.2 mm offset, jams at 3 mm; 11 tests pass (37 total)
note: contact params mix across geoms: steel solref 0.002 1 / solimp 0.95 0.99 0.0005 on parts AND receivers (a soft floor gave 3.6 mm penetration). Gate refined: pile drop at ~2 m/s penetrates 1.4 mm transiently, so gate is transient < 2 mm (no tunnelling through 4 mm walls) + resting < 0.5 mm. 3 mm-offset bolt jams tilted rather than resting on the rim.

title: V2 joint-torque sensor + Franka Hand taxel pads (src/fvb/sensors/)
result: static 1 kg load: tau_ext = J^T m g to 4e-7 relative (gate 2 %), F_ext_hat = (0, 0, 9.81) N; pressing a steel probe with 5 / 20 N: taxel sum 5.00 / 20.00 N (gate 5 %), all 16 taxels loaded; point contact CoP lands in the right taxel cell at 3 positions; pad shear sign and magnitude (3 N +- 0.3); force limit 70 N; 10 new tests (47 total)
note: tau_ext is computed from one forward pass (tau_J = actuator + passive + the joint's own frictionloss; model = M qacc + bias), so without noise it is exact: the 2 % gate only proves the plumbing; noise 0.05 Nm + per-episode bias 0.1 Nm (estimates, not Franka datasheet) and model mismatch are the real error sources. Fix found by the tests: the finger mesh's convex hull reached to 0.37 mm below the pad face, so pressed objects also touched the finger and part of the force bypassed the pad -> pads now protrude 1.5 mm. MuJoCo contact stiffness scales with effective mass: a 10 g probe at 5 N sank through the soft pad; part-like 100 g steel probes rest < 1 mm deep. Closed empty gripper: pads press each other (4 N) -> grasp detection in V3/V8 must not treat that as a grasp. Sensor read directly from qfrc_actuator instead of a jointactuatorfrc sensor (same quantity, no model edit). Also fixed: progress page counted commits in UTC (0 commits shown last hour).

title: V3 SortBoltsNuts env (src/fvb/envs/sort_bolts_nuts.py)
result: gate met by scripted forcing (9 tests, 56 total): seated bolt vanishes 1.0 s after first seated step; gripped bolt never vanishes; 12 deg tilted bolt in the chamfer never seats (6 deg rejected, 4 deg accepted by the rule); bolt standing beside the block (deep enough, wrong place) never counts, reward 0; nut dropped in bucket counts, nut on the rim / moving does not; 3 bolts + 3 nuts sorted -> outcome success, reward 1. Spawn: 20/20 seeds settle inside the bin (0/60 bolts land upright, all lie flat). 1 kHz physics, 20 Hz control: 15 ms per 50 ms step (3.3x real time) without cameras
note: joint torque + taxels sampled every physics step into 2 s ring buffers; obs torque_hist (10 x 15), tactile (max over the control interval), tau_ext; outcome/force_abort (|F_ext_hat| > 80 N)/timeout + dropped/jammed counts in info. Found while building: robosuite hides geom group 0 in cameras and takes inertia from group 0 only -> static scene geoms moved to group 1, parts get non-colliding group-1 visual twins; MuJoCo skips gravcomp unless a body has it at compile time -> vanished bolts are parked at rest on the floor 5 m away instead of floating. robosuite's agentview crops the bin and bucket -> added a 'sortview' front camera (deviation from the plan's agentview). Lowered-beside-the-block reward hack is a regression test from day one.

title: Joint-torque sampling moved after the full physics step
result: free-motion tau_ext max 1e-6 N m (was ~50 N phantom F_ext spikes every few steps, which tripped the 80 N force abort in free air); regression test added
note: robosuite 1.5 lite_physics runs mj_step1 -> _pre_action -> mj_step2, so at _pre_action qacc and actuator force still belonged to the previous state. Sampling now happens in _update_observables, right after each step.

title: Joint end-stop forces count as joint-internal in tau_J
result: a wrist rotation near joint 5's limit read 464 N m of 'external' torque; limit rows now go into tau_J like friction loss
note: a real Franka reflexes before the mechanical stop; the stop is inside the joint, not an external wrench

title: Tray instead of the plan's 80 mm bin (360 x 260 x 40 mm), spawn 60 mm from walls
result: the palm sits ~45 mm above the pad centre, so reaching a part near an 80 mm wall drove it into the wall (force abort); spawn check still 20/20 seeds settled
note: plan deviation (bin 300 x 220 x 80 in PLAN 13); documented in the env

title: V4 scripted expert (src/fvb/policy/sort_expert.py) - in progress
result: 0/8 full episodes so far (no noise); per part it now works end to end: nuts reach bucket A (5 of 8 seeds get >= 1 nut in), bolts are picked, turned head-up, servoed over the hole and dropped in (seated + vanished in seed 1). Episodes still end in the 80 N force abort, mostly bolt insertion / transport contacts
note: expert design: privileged pose tracking with OSC deltas; part-sized pre-grasp aperture; wall-clearance-scored grasp candidates (nut flats, bolt tilted about its shank up to 50 deg); fingertip floor clearance; stop descending at 25 N of estimated contact force; slow final 3 cm; least-rotation insertion approach; rate-limited insertion with stall -> spiral search; integral lateral term. Next: per-phase abort diagnosis on the 8 seeds, then noise, the >=90 % gate on unseen seeds, and recording 200 demos.

title: V4 expert: per-phase abort diagnosis, 4 rounds on 8 seeds
result: first full episode (seed 1: 6/6 sorted, 2232 steps = 112 s sim); seed 6 5/6; sorted parts over 8 seeds 0 -> 27/48. Remaining: nut grasps at the far tray side end with joint 6 at its 3.75 rad limit (fingers tilt into the floor), bolts dropped outside the tray are not re-picked
note: fixed, each from a measured abort: arm hit bucket A / fixture on a low transit (travel with the tip 10 cm up; bucket moved beside the tray to (-0.26, -0.46), the (0.15, 0.40) try stretched the arm to its F_hat-amplifying singularity); re-picking a nut still sliding in the bucket; fast descent (0.4 cap, 0.08 in the last 3 cm, touch stop 15 N); palm on the fixture (bolt grasped by its hex head); bolt pivoting in the grasp at chamfer contact (finger kp 1000 -> 4000, ~45 N grip, under the Hand's 70 N) and contact insertion replaced by hover 4 mm above the hole + drop when lateral < 0.7 mm and tilt < 2 deg (integral term only near the goal: it wound up in transit and overshot +-5 mm); gripper fully open before retreat (backing off dragged bolts out); joint-7-aware grasp yaw. Plan deviation: no spiral search (the drop needs no contact search).

title: V4 expert: home pose between parts, enter-then-release, return-to-tray
result: 3/8 full episodes (seeds 2, 5, 6; was 1/8), seed 3 5/6; sorted parts 27/48 -> 36/48 (no noise)
note: kept: return to the start pose between parts (the redundant arm drifted to joint 6's 3.75 rad limit after horizontal-hand moves); lower the aligned tip 8 mm into the hole before opening (dropping from the hover height let the slowly opening fingers push the bolt over); a bolt still held when a phase times out is carried back to the tray instead of dropped over the fixture. Tried and reverted: least-yaw grasp choice instead of the joint-7-aware one (1/8 full episodes vs 3/8). Env now reports MuJoCo bad-acceleration resets as outcome 'sim_unstable' (seen once with the reverted variant). Remaining: bolt top-down descents that still pin joint 6 (seeds 0, 4, 7), bolts lost to the table.

title: V4 expert: IK reachability for grasp choice; 16-seed A/B
result: 16 seeds, no noise: IK-filtered grasps 2/16 episodes, 54/96 parts; previous heuristic 2/16, 50/96 (outputs/v4_expert_ab/). Kept the IK version. Expert is far from the 90 % gate: ~55 % of parts sorted, and 90 % episodes needs ~98 % per part
note: finding: the palm-up/palm-down roll a bolt ends in is fixed by the grasp sign, and for one roll no insertion pose is reachable without a joint at its limit (IK: all 5 approach candidates at 0 margin vs 0.12-0.55 rad for the other roll). IK (damped least squares on a scratch MjData) now filters grasp candidates (joint margin > 0.15 rad at grasp and at the insertion pose); among feasible ones the least hand turn wins, tilt penalised. Tried: maximising the IK margin (picked 50 deg tilts, 1/8), fixed palm-down / palm-up (3/8, 0/8), rotation anchored between tray and hole (kept). Bug fixed: the grasp plan was recomputed at the start of the descent and could switch to a tilted grasp mid-way. Next: classify the 14 failed episodes by phase and fix the largest group; if per-part success stays far from 98 %, the task design (force-abort threshold, bolt presentation) is a question for the user.

title: V4 expert: failure census on 16 seeds, descend fixes
result: force aborts 9/16 -> 4/16, parts 54/96 -> 56-60/96 (two runs), full episodes 1-2/16. Plateau: per-part success ~60 %, the gate (90 % episodes) needs ~98 %
note: census of 14 failures: 7 finger collisions while descending (hand descended after the 'above' phase timed out -> now re-plans instead; 4 mm margin around the bolt head -> 44 mm pre-grasp; 6 mm OSC overshoot through the tray floor -> 6 mm floor margin; slower descent 0.25), 3 arm/hand hits on bucket A in transit (travel height +4 cm), 6 timeouts with bolts lost outside the tray (never re-picked) and parts skipped after 3 unreachable grasps. Contact forces jump from ~1 to 100-200 N within one 50 ms control step, so the 80 N abort cannot be avoided by a force check alone. Decision needed from the user (plan change): keep iterating the expert, present bolts upright (kitting rack), add a regrasp stand, or record demos per part from successful segments.

title: V4 expert: re-pick parts outside the tray; failed-attempt census
result: 16 seeds: 2/16 episodes (seed 9 now completes by re-picking a fallen bolt), 56-57/96 parts - unchanged plateau
note: kept: parts on the table / fixture top are re-picked (support surface per location; fixture block and bucket A added to the finger/palm clearance check), failed-attempt log, carry-back turns the hand towards pointing down (a horizontal-hand return locked joints 5-7 at their limits and every later attempt failed). Reverted: the 6 mm floor margin from the previous tick (pads rose above the 14.8 mm nuts -> 3 attempts, skipped) -> 3 mm. Each fix moves failures between buckets without lifting the total: waiting for the user's design decision (keep iterating / upright bolt rack / regrasp stand / per-part demos).

title: V4 demo recorder + pilot (8 noisy-expert episodes, 256^2 cameras)
result: recorder + validator kept (all 8 pilot episodes validate: schema, time, 2 x H.264 256^2 videos, segments; 263 MB for 8 episodes, ~30 ms per step with cameras). Pilot with human-like noise: 0/8 episodes, 17/48 parts; per-part segments 17/53 successful (bolts 6/29 attempts, nuts 11/24)
note: src/fvb/logging/sort_episode.py: data.npz (20 Hz low-dim incl. tau_ext, torque_hist 10x15, tactile 2x4x4, part status), one H.264 mp4 per camera, meta.json with per-part segments (start/end/success/sub-instruction) so a failed episode still yields the parts it sorted (option 4 of the pending decision). scripts/23_record_sort_demos.py writes ep_<seed>/ + index.jsonl. Pilot measures wall time per episode and the noisy expert's per-part rate.

title: V4 noisy expert: spiral search on missed entries, steadier fine phases
result: same 8 noisy seeds (no cameras): 1/8 episodes, 21/48 parts (was 0/8, 17/48)
note: the noisy hole estimate (sigma 1.5 mm) is about the whole entry tolerance (0.5 mm clearance + 1 mm chamfer); a missed entry used to retry the same point until timeout. Now each missed entry (chamfer force > 20 N or no depth after 4 s) moves the aim to the next point of a 0.7 mm-pitch spiral around the estimate - the plan's spiral search, now at the hover/drop level. Action jitter is scaled x0.3 in descend/close/hover/enter/let_go (an operator is steadier when precise). Design decision still pending.

title: V5 ACT (LeRobot) on 124 per-part demos, no force
result: trained 30k steps (loss 6.3 -> 0.20, l1 0.195). Closed loop on unseen seeds 5000-5009 (60 s each): 1 part(s) sorted / 60, outcomes ['force_abort', 'timeout']; policy latency 1.5 ms p50. 20k checkpoint: 0/24. Offline on a training episode: L1 error ~50 % of |action| (rotation dims ~100 %): underfit
note: the arm reaches into the tray (hand 17 mm above the floor) but never closes on a part (status never 'grasped'). Pipeline checked: recorded and served images share one orientation (robosuite renders upside down, both sides flip), same 16-D state. Cause is data: 124 per-part demos (~42k frames) of a long-horizon task, with the expert's deliberate jitter/pauses in the actions and ACT without language (it cannot be told which part). Reference result, as V5 has no bar; more / cleaner demos depend on the pending V4 decision.

title: ACT v2 + SmolVLA v1 on v1+v2 per-part demos (no force)
result: dataset outputs/lerobot/sort_v12_p1: 460 per-part episodes, 141404 frames (v1+v2). ACT v2 training (30k, batch 8). SmolVLA OOM'd at batch 16 next to ACT on the 9.65 GB GPU -> restarted at batch 8 / 30k steps (3.6 GB, ~0.37 s/step, ~3 h) | ACT v2 finished (30k, loss 0.189); SmolVLA v1 at 22k/30k | SmolVLA v1 finished 30k (loss 0.198). Closed loop: ACT v2 0/60, SmolVLA @20k 0/30; per-phase check (3 seeds x 600 steps each, final checkpoints): neither policy ever gets the pads within 3 cm of any part (closest 36-109 mm)
note: failure is at the approach, not the grasp: ACT moves ~3x less than the expert (mean |a| ~0.08 vs 0.2-0.3) - it averages the multimodal 'which part next' target of per-part segments from a cluttered tray into a hover; SmolVLA moves at expert scale but does not home in on a part from the 256^2 views. More of the same data is unlikely to fix this at our scale; a fixed, visually distinct target per segment (upright bolt rack / one part at a time) would.

title: ACT v2 20k-step checkpoint: closed-loop eval on seeds 5000-5009
result: ACT v2 @20k (460 per-part demos): 0/60 parts on seeds 5000-5009 (10 timeouts), same as ACT v1 (1/60)

title: Gripper deadband for learned policies (robosuite integrates sign(action))
result: gripper output snapped to the expert's -1 / 0 / +1 (|a| < 0.5 -> hold); unit test; ACT v2 final and SmolVLA v1 @20k ('put the nut in bucket A') evaluations running: first 4 episodes each 0 parts (some force aborts instead of timeouts) | SmolVLA v1 @20k done: 0/30 parts on seeds 5000-5004 (3 force aborts, 2 timeouts); ACT v2 still running | ACT v2 final: 0/60 parts (9 timeouts, 1 force abort)
note: the expert's gripper actions are exactly -1/0/+1 (45 % holds); PandaGripper adds 0.2*sign(a) per step, so a regressed 'hold' of +-0.02 drove the fingers open/closed with the sign of the noise.
